If your clothes dryer keeps running and won't shut off, here's what to do:

## Right now: stop it safely
1. **Open the door.** Almost every dryer has a door switch that cuts the drum and heat immediately.
2. If it still runs with the door open, or you smell burning, **unplug it** or **switch off its circuit breaker**. Gas dryers have the same breaker, and you can also close the gas shutoff valve behind the unit.
3. Let it cool before you poke around.

## Common causes
| Symptom | Likely culprit |
|---|---|
| Runs forever on **Auto/Sensor Dry**, clothes stay damp | Dirty **moisture sensor bars** (metal strips inside the drum, near the lint filter). Clean them with rubbing alcohol or a scrub pad, since fabric softener residue coats them. |
| Runs forever on Auto Dry, clothes are dry | Faulty moisture sensor or control board |
| **Timed Dry** never counts down (older dial dryers) | Failed **timer motor** |
| Keeps running even when **off or unplugged from settings**, or with the door open | **Stuck relay on the control board** or a shorted door/start switch |
| Takes very long, seems endless | **Clogged lint filter or vent**, which keeps clothes damp. Clean the filter and check that the outside vent flap blows strongly. This is also a fire risk. |

## Quick things to try
- Clean the lint screen and the moisture sensor bars.
- Use **Timed Dry** instead of Auto to see if the timer works.
- Unplug it for 5 minutes to reset the electronics.
- Check the outdoor vent for blockage.

## Call a technician if
- It runs with the door open or after being turned off, which points to the control board or relay.
- You smell burning or the outside of the dryer gets very hot.
- It's a gas dryer and you'd need to go inside the cabinet.

If you tell me the brand, the model, and whether it's a dial or a digital panel, I can narrow it down further.
its a Beko condenser. it stops if i open the door but turns again every few mins after it says End

That's almost certainly normal. It's the **anti-crease feature**, not a fault.

## What's happening
After the cycle finishes and shows "End", Beko condenser dryers turn the drum briefly every few minutes so clothes don't settle and wrinkle while sitting warm in the drum. On most Beko models this lasts **up to about 2 hours**, then stops on its own.

## How to stop it
- **Open the door**, take the clothes out, and **press the On/Off button** (or turn the dial to Off). It won't restart once switched off.
- **Turn it off for future loads:** many Beko models have an **"Anti-Creasing"** or **"Anti-Crease"** option button (sometimes a shirt icon) that you can press before starting. On some models it's always on and can't be disabled. Your manual will say which applies to yours.

## When it would be a real problem
- The drum keeps turning **long after 2 hours**
- It turns with **the dryer switched off**
- It **heats** during those turns (anti-crease is cold tumbling only)

If none of those apply, your dryer is fine. If you share the model number (on a sticker inside the door rim), I can tell you whether it has the anti-crease off option.
